beforeDefinition: Same profiling/echo implementation, before bounded reply coalescing. Reconstruct with baseline-reply.patch in a separate experimental checkout.
afterDefinition: Fixed 3856-byte response submitted through one write_all plus flush.
environment: Shared Windows development laptop. Other task benchmarks, builds and tests paused during capture. OS scheduling, CPU accounting precision and thermal state uncontrolled.
metadataNormalization: Saturated reports renamed rustCpuCounter.resolutionMs to counterUnitMs after capture and added a precision caveat. No timing, CPU, memory or event-count value was changed.

limitations: Raw repeats, no performance pass/fail threshold; inspect their range, not one favorable run.
Batch latency includes scheduling from common submission until mix/FFmpeg stdin acceptance, not audible output.
Paced batches use common 20ms deadlines without unbounded catch-up queues. No provider decode or network is modeled.
Pipeline CPU sums parent, owned Rust counter deltas and FFmpeg diagnostics; counter resolution and accounting uncertainty apply.
Echo isolates aggregate protocol/copy/pipe/scheduling costs; do not subtract independent p99s to estimate pure mix latency.
RSS fields are process lifetime peaks, not simultaneous whole-tree peak. FFmpeg RSS can be unavailable.
